name: Halvek Tamarind-Chili Fruit Coins
description: Flat, ridged hard candy coins in tamarind-chili flavor, pressed with the Halvek sunburst logo. Long-lasting and intensely flavored, sold in roll packaging at nearly every transit kiosk in Meridian 88.
flavor_profile: Sour tamarind and dried fruit sweetness with a slow-building chili warmth; the hard candy lasts eight to twelve minutes; slight salt finish from added electrolytes
cultural_context: Halvek coins are so ubiquitous they've become almost invisible — the candy equivalent of background noise. Finding a Halvek roll at the bottom of a bag is universally relatable. The sunburst logo is sometimes used as slang for anything mass-produced and reliable but uninspiring: 'It's fine, it's very Halvek.'
story_hooks: A Halvek factory worker has discovered that a production run was contaminated with a batch of unlicensed stim compound — and the product has already shipped
Someone is counterfeiting Halvek rolls with near-identical packaging containing a different, cheaper formula; the brand is hemorrhaging trust without knowing why

A transit kiosk operator who sells Halvek coins has been using the kiosk as a message relay point for years — the coins themselves are sometimes the message, with specific roll configurations signaling coded information
